title: Log cabin square — basic
subtitle: A square built by crocheting strips around a central rectangle, log-cabin style
excerpt: The log cabin square starts with a small foundation rectangle at the centre and adds a strip along each of its four sides in turn, rotating the work 90 degrees after each strip. Four strips in two alternating colours give a geometric square that measures 12 cm across with no corners to fill or chain spaces to navigate.
sourceNotes: Log cabin construction originates in patchwork quilting (documented from the 1860s); the crochet equivalent is described in Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), strip-built motif chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A log cabin crochet square in cream and warm terracotta DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Concentric rectangular strips visible from the centre, 12 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished log cabin square measures 12 × 12 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Log cabin square — basic
chartDefinition.caption: Centre rectangle worked first in colour A. Strips added in rotation — one side at a time — alternating colour A and colour B.

glossaryTerms.definition: A row of double crochet worked along one edge of an existing piece, adding width on that side before the work is rotated to add the next strip on an adjacent edge.

content.text: The log cabin square grows outward from a central rectangle by adding a

along each side in rotation. After four strips, the block is a square. After eight, it is larger. The construction never requires working into a chain space or managing a corner cluster — it is just rows.
Two colours alternate so each pair of opposite strips reads the same. The block joins flat at any edge and stacks into blankets without gaps between the motifs.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 6 g colour A and 6 g colour B in DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Ch 7. Dc in 2nd ch from hook and in each ch to end. Turn. (6 dc.) Work 3 more rows in dc. Fasten off. (4-row rectangle, 6 sts wide.)
Join colour B to the right edge of the rectangle. Work 1 dc into each row-end along the right side (4 dc). Turn. Work 1 more row in dc. Fasten off.

Rotate the work 90 degrees after each strip. Strip 2 (colour A): work along the top edge including the new Strip 1 corner. Strip 3 (colour B): work along the left edge. Strip 4 (colour A): work along the bottom edge. The block is now square. Continue adding 4-strip rounds until the motif is the size you need.
Work the four-colour log cabin square for a different colour in each of the four quadrants. Or try the textured version, which alternates dc rows with htr rows for a ridged surface.
